title: Controlling Incompatible Magic: Ontology-Conditioned Activation Steering in a Fantasy Landscape
description: Language models operating within a specified conceptual world may substitute familiar mechanisms for those permitted by the supplied rules. This research protocol investigates whether contrastive activation steering improves operational consistency with a causal ontology beyond structured prompting, and whether an intervention remains useful when the ontology changes. We define a synthetic fantasy world with class-restricted actions, finite energy, conserved object identity, and bounded transformations. Two versions differ in the availability of a narrowly constrained local rewind operation. A deterministic benchmark contains 720 cases across nine scenario families and distinguishes permitted but infeasible actions from prohibited and undefined capabilities. Version-specific steering directions will be estimated from matched training responses and evaluated against identical prompt-only, stale-direction, zero-coefficient, and norm-matched random controls. The primary outcome combines correct classification with legal goal-reaching execution; secondary outcomes measure task performance, unknown-concept recognition, and suppression of newly valid temporal plans. Hyperparameters will be selected on development data and fixed before held-out evaluation. The pilot has only three independent test families, so its uncertainty estimates will be exploratory. Model-performance experiments have not yet been conducted. The protocol provides a controlled test of the benefits and limitations of activation steering under changing causal rules, without assuming that improved output consistency implies removal of internal concepts.
notes: Research protocol preprint, version 0.1.0; not peer reviewed. Pretrained-model experiments and their results are pending.
